_meta.indication: Unituxin (dinutuximab) is a GD2-binding monoclonal antibody indicated, in combination with GM-CSF, IL-2, and 13-cis-retinoic acid (RA), for the treatment of pediatric patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who achieve at least a partial response to prior first-line multiagent, multimodality therapy

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), open-label, multicenter, active-controlled trial comparing dinutuximab immunotherapy + RA versus standard therapy with RA alone
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who achieved CR, VGPR, or PR following induction and myeloablative therapy with autologous stem cell rescue
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Event-free survival (EFS), the prespecified primary endpoint; overall survival (OS) was a key secondary endpoint
pivotal_trials.n: 226 eligible patients randomized (113 dinutuximab/RA arm, 113 RA-alone arm); study terminated after accrual of 226 of 386 planned patients
pivotal_trials.result: EFS improved 42% (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.37, 0.89; p=0.01 by log-rank); median EFS not reached (dinutuximab) vs 1.9 years (control). OS was a key secondary endpoint and showed only a trend in improved overall survival (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.37, 0.91), not formally demonstrated as statistically significant

nct_ctgov.title: Isotretinoin With or Without Dinutuximab, Aldesleukin, and Sargramostim Following Stem Cell Transplant in Treating Patients With Neuroblastoma

key_safety: Most common ADRs (>=25%): pain, pyrexia, thrombocytopenia, lymphopenia, infusion reactions, hypotension, hyponatremia, increased ALT, anemia. Serious/life-threatening infusion reactions occurred in 26% of patients; severe (Grade 3) pain in 68 (51%) of the Unituxin/RA group; severe (Grade 3 or 4) hypotension in 22 (16%); severe (Grade 3-5) capillary leak syndrome in 31 (23%)
target_moa: Chimeric monoclonal antibody that binds specifically to the GD2 disialoganglioside expressed on neuroblastoma, inducing complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) and antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS INFUSION REACTIONS AND NEUROPATHY. Life-threatening infusion reactions occur with Unituxin (administer prehydration/premedication, interrupt for severe reactions, discontinue for anaphylaxis); Unituxin causes severe neuropathic pain requiring IV opioid administration.

rems.type: A REMS is not required to ensure safe use; treatment is limited to pediatric oncologists at tertiary or specialized medical centers familiar with these risks

advisory_committee.vote: This BLA was not the subject of an advisory committee meeting; the review team instead sought advice from two pediatric oncology consultants and one patient representative

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted for dinutuximab on December 20, 2010 for the treatment of neuroblastoma

citations.quote: Orphan drug designation was granted for dinutuximab on December 20, 2010, for the treatment of neuroblastoma, therefore dinutuximab is exempt from the requirements of the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA).

basis.text: The BLA received Priority review designation

summary.text: Unituxin received Priority review and had Orphan Drug designation (granted December 20, 2010 for neuroblastoma); it was approved on the original BLA based on a randomized, open-label, multicenter trial (Study ANBL0032/DIV-NB-301) demonstrating a 42% improvement in event-free survival with a trend in improved overall survival. It was not approved under accelerated approval and was not the subject of an advisory committee meeting.

requirement.text: 2878-1: Study to compare exposure and safety data from ~220 patients completing dinutuximab treatment, pooled across lots, with historical experience in ~1100 patients treated with ch14.18 manufactured by SAIC for the NCI, to analyze risk of serious infusion reactions and neuropathy

citations.quote: **2878-1** Conduct a study to compare exposure and safety data from approximately 220 patients who complete treatment with dinutuximab, pooling across dinutuximab lots and by individual lot, with the historical experience observed in approximately 1100 patients treated with ch14.18 (manufactured by SAIC for the National Cancer Institute).

requirement.text: 2878-2: Study to analyze laboratory data (serum complement, IgE, tryptase, histamine, human anti-chimeric antibody) in patients with Grade 4 allergic reactions or anaphylaxis to better characterize these adverse reactions

citations.quote: **2878-2** Conduct a study to analyze laboratory data including serum complement, IgE, tryptase, histamine, and human anti-chimeric antibody levels obtained in patients with documented Grade 4 allergic reactions or anaphylaxis from a sufficient number of patients with neuroblastoma to allow for improved characterization of these adverse reactions to better inform product labeling.

requirement.text: 2878-3: Develop and validate an assay with improved sensitivity for detection of neutralizing antibodies against dinutuximab in the presence of expected dinutuximab levels

citations.quote: **2878-3** Develop and validate an assay with improved sensitivity for the detection of neutralizing antibodies against dinutuximab in the presence of dinutuximab levels that are expected to be present in samples at the time of patient sampling.

requirement.text: 2878-4: Study to assess neutralizing anti-drug antibody responses to dinutuximab with a validated assay in at least 300 patients, with interim and final reports from Studies DIV-NB-302, DIV-NB-303, DIV-NB-201 and NANT2011-04

citations.quote: **2878-4** To conduct a study to assess the neutralizing anti-drug antibody responses to dinutuximab with a validated assay capable of sensitively detecting neutralizing antibody responses in the presence of dinutuximab levels that are expected to be present in the blood at the time of patient sampling. The clinical impact of the neutralizing antibody response should be evaluated in at least 300 patients to include an interim report analyzing data from Studies DIV-NB-302, DIV-NB-303 and DIV-NB-201 and a final report analyzing data from Study NANT2011-04.

requirement.text: 2878-5: Conduct a 5-month repeat-dose juvenile animal toxicology study in cynomolgus monkeys measuring chronic toxicity of dinutuximab, particularly effects on the central and peripheral nervous system

citations.quote: **2878-5** To conduct a 5-month repeat-dose juvenile animal toxicology study in cynomolgus monkeys that will measure the chronic toxicity of dinutuximab, particularly its effects on the central and peripheral nervous system.
